grade_reason: The only AI material found is undated campaign copy treating AI as a military and economic matter (AI in warfare, AI development jobs); nothing found on catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: 7 web searches ran, none refused. No direct, dated quote by Bennett on AI was found. Her campaign national security page (https://rebeccabennettforcongress.com/priorities/protecting-americas-national-security/, read 2026-11-14, undated) says "The use of new and improving technologies, including AI and drones, are only making the world more dangerous" and pledges to "Prepare the United States for 21st century warfare" including "drone warfare, and the use of AI in international conflicts"; this is military use of AI (ruling 3) and general danger without a catastrophic harm named, so D. Her economy page (https://rebeccabennettforcongress.com/priorities/growing-new-jerseys-economy/, undated, images from 2025) pledges to "Ensure New Jersey is a national leader in clean energy, biotech, AI development, and high-tech jobs" (promoting AI, D). Both are undated campaign copy, so left out of statements. The only AI news item about her (New Jersey Monitor, 28 May 2026, https://newjerseymonitor.com/2026/05/28/campaign-mailer-house-election-ai/) concerns a likely doctored image of her in an outside group's mailer, not her views. A New Jersey Monitor article on NJ Democrats and AI/data center regulation (https://newjerseymonitor.com/?p=25371) returned 403 and could not be checked for Bennett remarks. As a non-member she could not have co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. Results for other Bennetts (Michael Timothy Bennett, Clay Bennett) were ignored. If the reviewer considers this campaign copy not to be statements about AI, the grade should be 'none'.
